BẮT ĐẦU TẠI ĐÂY
widgets_values:
Singularity V2 từ workflow đã cung cấp. Dùng PREPARE.bat để chọn storyboard và sheet rồi tự sinh prompt + dây nối cùng thứ tự. Không cần cắt grid.
Bước false: tạo nháp và lưu take. Xem nháp; đổi bước true rồi chạy để nâng take đã chọn.
Bản cho RTX 4060 Ti tắt sparse / Kitchen attention và LoRA người thật. Đây là lựa chọn tương thích, chưa benchmark GPU.

widgets_values_named.text:
# MiniMax-H3 Turbo - Speed + Quality
### tuned for your RTX 5070 Ti (16 GB)

## Two paths, one switch
The red **USE REFERENCE IMAGES** boolean picks which path runs:

- **false = PATH A** - text-to-video, image-to-video, first-last-frame
- **true = PATH B** - reference-to-video (your images define the subject)

The switch is **lazy**: only the selected path is ever executed, so the
unused branch costs you nothing - no second prompt encode, no image load.

## Shared controls (gold nodes)
One **PROMPT** box feeds both paths - you never edit the wrong one.
**resolution + aspect ratio** and **duration (seconds)** also feed both.

`prompt`, `width`, `height` and `length` on the two path nodes are **driven
sockets** - greyed out on purpose. Set them from the gold nodes. Only PATH B
`width` and `height` stay at 1792 x 992: they size the references. Leave them.

## The three speed levers (green nodes)
1. **4-step Turbo LoRA** - ~20 steps becomes **4 steps**. Biggest single win.
2. **Model Sparse Attention** (`sol-attn`, tau 1.3) - training-free sparse
   attention. The gain grows with sequence length.
3. **Comfy Kitchen attention** - INT8 dense attention, used wherever sparse
   attention is inactive (the first 20% of steps, and the sink rows).

## Dials that matter
- **steps** (`BasicScheduler`) - 4 is the LoRA trained point. 6 is cleaner.
  The scheduler stays on `simple`.
- **LoRA strength** - 1.0. Blurry or ghosting, raise to 1.05-1.15.
  Over-sharp or plastic-looking, lower to 0.85-0.95.
- **tau** (sparse node) - higher is sparser and faster, lower quality.
  1.3 is the sweet spot, 1.0 is safer, 1.6-1.8 is faster.
- **start_percent 0.2** - the first 20% of steps stay dense. Do not set to 0.

## First run is slow
The text encoder (~15.7 GB) loads, encodes, unloads; then the DiT (~21 GB)
streams in. Triton kernels also compile on first use. Judge speed from the
**second** run onward.

nodes.title: CÁCH DÙNG HAI BƯỚC
widgets_values:
1. BƯỚC = false → Chạy → xem video nháp; take lưu output/h3_takes.
2. Chọn take cụ thể nếu có nhiều tác vụ; latest lấy take mới nhất khi chạy.
3. BƯỚC = true → Chạy → nâng take, không cần encode storyboard lại.
Âm thanh được giữ từ bước 1; bản vá audio-freeze được bộ cài áp dụng có kiểm tra, không cần Node.js.
Color Transfer chỉ bước 2; finishing cả hai bước. Đây là nâng latent + refine, không phải FlashVSR.

widgets_values_named.text:
# Preview first, then upscale only the good ones

## STEP 1 - make the video  (STEP = `false`)
1. Set **STEP** to `false`.
2. Click **Run**. MiniMax makes the video at your base size and
   **VIDEO OUT** shows it. Nothing is upscaled.
3. Every run also saves a **take** (the pass 1 latent + its prompt and
   reference data) to `output\h3_takes`. The names match:
   - take `MiniMaxH3_take_00007_`
   - video `video\MiniMaxH3_take_00007_preview_00001_.mp4`
4. Don't like it? Click **Run** again. The seed is on `randomize`, so
   every run is a new take.

## STEP 2 - upscale the one you like  (STEP = `true`)
1. Set **STEP** to `true`.
2. **which take**: `latest` = the video you just made. For an older one,
   press **R** (refreshes the list), then pick its number.
3. Click **Run**. Only the upscale runs - no pass 1, no text encoder,
   no reference images. Out comes
   `video\MiniMaxH3_take_00007_UPSCALED_00001_.mp4`.
4. Set **STEP** back to `false` for the next video.

## Good to know
- A take keeps its own prompt and reference data. You can change the
  prompt for the next shot and still upscale an older take correctly.
- Pass 2 settings (**UPSCALE TARGET** megapixels, steps + denoise, time
  chunks) are read in step 2, so you can upscale the same take again with
  other settings without making it again.
- Don't want to watch? **Run** with STEP = `false`, flip to `true`, **Run**
  again. `latest` is picked when that job starts, so it upscales the take
  made just before it.
- Step 2 uses the models in this workflow (MiniMax model, Turbo LoRA,
  attention), so keep them the same as when the take was made.
- A take is roughly 50-150 MB. Delete old ones from
  `ComfyUI-Shared\output\h3_takes` when you don't need them.
- **Transfer Color** (dark red node under VIDEO OUT) runs in step 2 only. It matches the
  upscaled colours to the pass 1 take, so the upscale is not more contrasty.
  Set to 1.0: the full match.
- **FINISHING** (green node under VIDEO OUT) runs in both steps, after Transfer Color.
  It sharpens (`detail_contrast` +0.55 at radius 0.2), softly rolls off the brightest whites,
  and `shadow_lift` 0.05 opens the crushed blacks, in both steps, so draft and upscale match.
  Too crisp? 0.35. Do not set `detail_contrast` negative. Too flat? `shadow_lift` 0.03.
- Step 1 makes a **0.2 MP draft** - small and fast, just to judge motion and
  framing. Step 2 adds detail with a gentle 4-step repaint and keeps the motion and mouths.
- **UPSCALE TARGET** 2 MP (about 1888x1088). 1.0 MP makes step 2 about
  2-3x faster. Soft result? Use the 5-step sigmas preset.
- The take nodes come from `ComfyUI\custom_nodes\comfyui-h3-take`.
- **Pass 2 needs the audio-freeze patch** (`patch_h3_upscale_audio_freeze.js`, run once).
  It makes the untiled MMH3 Ultimate Upscale keep the pass 1 audio fixed, so lips follow
  the sound you hear instead of new speech the model makes up and then throws away.
- **Keep TILE PASS 2 = `false` with `er_sde`.** `er_sde` adds fresh noise every step,
  which is what rebuilds knit, hair and skin texture. The tiled branch runs one sampler
  call per step, so it needs `euler`, which comes out smooth - use it only for OOM.
- **CLARITY** (under FINISHING) adds mid-size local contrast (radius 0.6% of height,
  +0.1) for depth on faces, hair and fabric. It is kept low on purpose: this is the node that
  makes the upscale look harder than the draft.

Nháp 0.2 MP, nâng 0.7 MP ban đầu; tăng sau khi chạy ổn. Chiều rộng/cao bội 32; frame 17n+5 ở 24 FPS. 15 giây → 362 frame. Local dùng tối đa 15 giây/lượt; tập dài chia nhiều lượt.
Encoder NVFP4 được giải lượng tử khi tính trên RTX 40: không có tăng tốc FP4 phần cứng như RTX 50. Cần RAM/pagefile và dung lượng trống phù hợp; không có bảo đảm 16 GB đủ mọi cấu hình.

widgets_values_named.text:
# Resolution, aspect ratio, duration

## Quality tiers
The **Resolution Selector** sets aspect ratio + quality. The `megapixels`
dial is the quality select - these are the standard MiniMax P tiers:

| tier | megapixels | 16:9 output |
|---|---|---|
| **360P (loaded now - draft)** | **0.2** | **608 x 352** |
| 416P | 0.3 | 736 x 416 |
| 480P | 0.4 | 864 x 480 |
| 540P | 0.5 | 960 x 544 |
| 640P | 0.7 | 1152 x 640 |
| 720P | 0.9 | 1280 x 736 |
| 768P | 1.0 | 1376 x 768 |
| 832P | 1.2 | 1504 x 832 |
| 928P | 1.5 | 1664 x 928 |
| 1024P | 1.8 | 1824 x 1024 |
| 1080P | 2.0 | 1920 x 1088 |

Pass 1 is now a **0.2 MP draft** - pass 2 makes the final size.
For a draft with more detail use 0.3-0.4. Above ~1.0 expect heavy
disk paging and very long runs.

## Aspect ratios
`1:1` - `2:3` - `3:2` - `3:4` - `4:3` - `9:16` - `16:9` - `21:9`

**Leave `multiple` on 32.** MiniMax-H3 requires both sides to be a multiple
of 32 - 8 or 16 will error out.

## Duration is in seconds
Snapped **up** to the nearest length the model accepts:

| you type | real clip | frames |
|---|---|---|
| 3 s | 3.04 s | 73 |
| 4 s | 4.46 s | 107 |
| **5 s** | **5.17 s** | **124** |
| 6 s | 6.58 s | 158 |
| 8 s | 8.00 s | 192 |
| 10 s | 10.13 s | 243 |

Trained range is roughly 5 s to 15 s.

## If you run out of memory
**16 GB VRAM, 23 GB system RAM** against ~37 GB of weights - Windows **will**
page to disk. That is expected. In order:
1. Drop `megapixels` one tier (0.7 -> 0.5 -> 0.4).
2. Drop duration to 4 s, then 3 s.
3. Raise `tau` to 1.6.
4. On Path B, use fewer reference images.

## 0.2 MP and sparse attention
`min_tokens` on the sparse node is **8192**. At 0.2 MP a clip shorter than
about 7 s has fewer tokens than that, so pass 1 runs dense. That is fine - the
draft is so small that dense attention is already fast. Pass 2 (2 MP) is far
above 8192, so sparse attention still speeds up the expensive part.

## Why not the MiniMax-H3 Turbo LoRA node?
Your LoRA keys are already prefixed with `diffusion_model.`. That node
re-prefixes them, so it would match **zero** weights and silently do nothing.
`LoraLoaderModelOnly` matches them correctly. Keep it as it is.

nodes.title: ĐỒNG BỘ ẢNH VỚI PROMPT
widgets_values:
Picture 1 luôn là nguyên storyboard. Picture 2 trở đi chỉ là ảnh đang bật trong project.json, được PREPARE.bat đánh số và nối cùng lúc.
Muốn thêm/bỏ ảnh: sửa assets[].enabled trong project rồi chạy PREPARE lại. Không Ctrl+B ảnh trực tiếp mà giữ prompt cũ. Asset tắt dùng mô tả và storyboard, không giả có character sheet.

widgets_values_named.text:
# PATH B - Reference to Video

Set **USE REFERENCE IMAGES** to `true`, then load your images into
**reference image 1 / 2**. The model uses them as the *identity and style*
source, not as a first frame - the subject is re-rendered in new motion.

## Referring to them in the prompt
The references are numbered in socket order. Mention them explicitly:

> `<Picture 1>` wearing a red jacket walks through the neon alley from
> `<Picture 2>`, handheld camera, shallow depth of field.

Without a mention the model still absorbs style, but naming them is far more
reliable for identity.

## Adding more references
Connect a third image and a **fourth empty socket appears by itself** - the
ref sockets grow as you fill them. There are also sockets for a reference
**video** (`ref_video_0`) and reference **audio** (`ref_audio_0`) - a voice
sample there carries the timbre into the generated audio.

## ref_image_size
- `match` (loaded) - shrinks each reference to the `width` x `height` on this
  node, never enlarges it. Those are 1792 x 992 and only size the references:
  the video size comes from **PASS 1 empty latent**.
- Leave them. At 960 x 544 a face in a character sheet is about 100 px wide,
  so the model has no skin detail to copy and faces come out soft.
- `max` - up to 2048 px on the short edge. Much slower.
- Size is set when the take is made. Old takes keep their small references:
  run step 1 again to get the benefit.

## A note on your LoRA
Your turbo LoRA is `minimax_h3_**ref2v**_lightx2v_turbo_4step` - it was
distilled on the reference-to-video path specifically. So Path B is the
path this particular LoRA is most at home on.

## Path A is still there
Set the boolean back to `false` and Path A runs unchanged. The two Load
Image nodes in Path A stay bypassed for pure text-to-video.

widgets_values_named.text:
# Latent Upscale - pass 2
Pass 1 renders exactly like before. Pass 2 takes the finished latent, upscales
the **video** with the **MiniMax-H3 3D latent upscaler**, then re-samples it at
the bigger size with 4 gentle steps, so the take's motion and mouths stay. The **audio is never touched** -
it is still decoded straight from pass 1.

## The dials
| node | what it sets |
|---|---|
| **resolution + aspect ratio** (gold, top) | pass 1 size - its `megapixels` is the size the video is **created** at |
| **UPSCALE TARGET** `megapixels` | the size it is **upscaled** to. Aspect ratio follows pass 1 by itself |
| **STEP** (top right, next to VIDEO OUT) | `false` = step 1: make the video and save its take. `true` = step 2: upscale a saved take |
| **UPSCALER?** | `true` = H3 3D latent upscaler model. `false` = plain latent interpolation (no model, softer - give it more denoise) |
| **PASS 2 - steps + denoise** | how much pass 2 repaints (table below) |
| **pass 2 seed** | noise for pass 2 only. Left on `fixed` so pass 2 is repeatable |
| **TIME CHUNKS** `chunk_length` | pass 2 samples long clips in overlapping pieces so they fit in 16 GB |
| **TILE PASS 2?** | `true` = also split each piece into tiles. Only if you still run out of VRAM |

The **upscale size report** node prints the exact size you get,
for example `1280x736  ->  1888x1088`.

## Megapixels -> real size (16:9)
| created at | upscale 1.5 | upscale 2.0 | upscale 2.5 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.4 (864x480) | 1664x928 | 1952x1088 | 2176x1216 |
| 0.5 (960x544) | 1696x960 | 1920x1088 | 2144x1216 |
| 0.7 (1152x640) | 1664x928 | 1952x1088 | 2176x1216 |
| 0.9 (1280x736, multiple 32) | 1664x960 | 1888x1088 | 2112x1216 |
| **0.9 (1280x720, multiple 40) - loaded** | 1664x928 | **1920x1088 - loaded** | 2176x1216 |

The target must be bigger than pass 1 - the upscaler refuses to shrink.

## PASS 2 - SIGMAS (how much pass 2 repaints)
The first number is how much of the take gets redrawn. Starting at 0.90 keeps
about 10% of it: the layout survives, but mouths and expressions are made up
again. 0.55 keeps about 45%, enough to hold them. To use another line, paste
it into the **PASS 2 - SIGMAS** box:

| preset | sigmas | use it for |
|---|---|---|
| **4 steps, motion lock (loaded)** | `0.5500, 0.4200, 0.3158, 0.1579, 0.0000` | default - mouths and motion stay |
| 3 steps | `0.9035, 0.6316, 0.3158, 0.0000` | fastest, re-acts the scene |
| 4 steps, face detail | `0.9035, 0.6316, 0.3158, 0.1579, 0.0000` | re-acts the scene: mouths move on their own |
| 4 steps, old | `0.9035, 0.8000, 0.6316, 0.3158, 0.0000` | softer faces: the last step jumps from 0.3158 straight to 0 |
| 5 steps | `0.9035, 0.8000, 0.6316, 0.3158, 0.1579, 0.0000` | most detail, about 25% slower |
| gentle | `0.7200, 0.5500, 0.2700, 0.0000` | old behaviour - only for a 0.5 MP+ pass 1 |

Steps cost time, denoise does not: 4 steps at 0.90 takes as long as
4 steps at 0.25.
The sampler is `er_sde` (pass 2 sampler node).

## VRAM / RAM (16 GB / 23 GB)
Tokens per forward = (width/32) x (height/32) x latent frames in the piece.
A 136-frame chunk is 40 latent frames:
- pass 1 now, 1280x736, whole 15 s clip: **98,440**
- pass 2, 1888x1088, one 136-frame chunk: **80,240**

A 15 s clip becomes 3 overlapping chunks. Clips of 136 frames or less
(5.67 s) run as a single piece automatically.

If pass 2 runs out of memory, in this order:
1. `chunk_length` 136 -> 102 -> 68 (always a multiple of 17).
2. **TILE PASS 2?** = `true` (auto grid, at most `token_budget` tokens per tile).
3. Lower the **UPSCALE TARGET** megapixels.

Decoded frames sit in system RAM: 15 s at 1888x1088 is about 8.3 GB,
so expect Windows to page. The first pass 2 at a new size also compiles
new Triton kernels, so judge its speed from the second run.

## Preview first, then upscale only the good ones
Pass 2 no longer re-renders pass 1. Step 1 saves every video's pass 1 as a
take on disk; step 2 upscales a take you pick. See the
**HOW TO - preview first, then upscale** note next to **STEP** (top right).

## Good to know
- Pass 2 uses the prompt + references saved in the take, not the PROMPT box.
- Path B references ride along into pass 2 unchanged.
- Path A first/last-frame images: pass 2 reuses those keyframes, resized in
  latent space to the new size.
- The `upscale size report` fills in after a run.

## Model file
`minimax_h3_latent_upscaler_3d_fp16.safetensors` lives in
`ComfyUI-Shared\models\latent_upscale_models`
(huggingface.co/LBH-123-AI/Minimax_h3_latent_Upscaler).
The MMH3 upscaler nodes only look in that first `latent_upscale_models` folder.

subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the seaside station in <Picture 1>: a sunny platform, the red-brick building with a white canopy, and a silver train with a blue stripe and no lettering, doors open. Every shot looking along the platform faces the same way as <Picture 1>: building on the left, train on the right.
<Subject 2> is Leo, 20, from <Picture 2> (face: top-row portraits; body and outfit: bottom row): short messy dark-brown curls close to his head, dark brown eyes, clean-shaven, lean runner's build, a heather-grey T-shirt, black running shorts, grey running shoes, a black watch on his left wrist. He holds a flat brown leather sketchbook the size of a hardback, with no strap in his right hand.
<Subject 3> is Maya, 19, from <Picture 3> (face: top-row portraits; body and outfit: bottom row): long wavy chestnut-brown hair, hazel eyes, light freckles, fair skin, an oversized cream cable-knit cardigan over a white T-shirt, light-blue jeans, white sneakers, small gold hoops, an olive-green tote on her right shoulder. She has a small dark-green rolling suitcase beside her.

summary:
[reference generation] At <Subject 1>, <Subject 3> waits by an open train door and finds her sketchbook missing. Far down the platform, <Subject 2> bursts out of the station doorway with it and runs toward her, calling out.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (all shots): fully_preserved - the platform, building, canopy and stationary train in the same morning light.
<Subject 2> ([Shot 3], [Shot 4]): fully_preserved - one Leo as in <Picture 2>, without the sheet's layout.
<Subject 3> ([Shot 1], [Shot 2], [Shot 5]): fully_preserved - one Maya as in <Picture 3>, without the sheet's layout.

detailed_description:
A photorealistic live-action British romance film, real actors with natural skin texture, anamorphic cinema lenses, crisp focus on faces, fine film grain, a honey-gold and sea-blue grade; a clear, bright late-spring morning just before eight: warm sunlight, soft shadows, a pale-blue sky. Daylight throughout.
[Shot 1] A wide shot along the platform of <Subject 1>, building on the left, train on the right. The train is parked and stays completely stationary, fixed in the frame. <Subject 3>, the chestnut-haired young woman in the cream cardigan, stands in the right foreground beside an open train door with the green suitcase, her back to the camera, looking down the platform toward the station doorway in the distance on the left. Further along, two passengers step aboard. At 00:00.500, an off-screen female station announcer (S1) says calmly over the speaker, <d>[English] The train on platform two is about to depart.</d> The camera holds a static shot.
[Shot 2] At 00:03.500, cut to a medium close-up of <Subject 3>, the chestnut-haired young woman, standing on the platform with the open train door behind her. She rummages in her olive tote, pulls it wider and searches again; her face falls. She looks to her left down the platform, lips pressed together. The camera holds a static shot.
[Shot 3] At 00:07.000, cut to the same wide view along the platform as the first shot, building on the left, train on the right; she is just out of frame on the right, beside the camera. In the distance, <Subject 2>, the curly-haired young man in the grey T-shirt, bursts out of the station doorway on the left and runs along the platform toward the camera, then slows, chest heaving, the sketchbook in his right hand. The platform between him and the camera is empty. The camera holds a static shot.
[Shot 4] At 00:10.000, cut to a medium close-up of <Subject 2>, the curly-haired young man, now close to the camera, the canopy and building behind him on the left, the train on the right, nobody else in frame. He sees her just beside the lens and lifts the sketchbook toward her. At 00:10.600, <Subject 2> (S2) calls out in a warm, husky young man's voice, soft English accent, breathless, <d>[English] Wait!</d> The camera holds a static shot.
[Shot 5] At 00:12.500, cut to a close-up of <Subject 3>, the chestnut-haired young woman, still standing on the platform, the open train door behind her, turning toward his voice. Her lips part in surprise and a slow smile begins. The camera pushes in slowly with small amplitude.
Leo and Maya never share a voice. Each character is one real person with the same face in every shot. Real physics: hair and clothes move only slightly, hands grip objects firmly. Understated, natural acting; nobody looks into the lens. Each line starts at its written time at a natural pace; pauses are held as silence. No other dialogue is spoken at any point. No text, subtitles or watermark.

overall_soundscape:
The idling train hums and birds chirp under the canopy. Canvas rustles as she searches her bag. Running footsteps burst onto the platform and slow, then hard breathing.

widgets_values_named.text:
# Singularity v2 - low-res draft + strong upscale

Same workflow, same two steps (make a take, then upscale it).
What is new in v2:

| node | v1 | v2 |
|---|---|---|
| resolution + aspect ratio `megapixels` | 0.5 | **0.2** (draft) |
| SIGMA SHIFT (new, green) | - (shift 12 / 3) | **6 / 3** |
| sampler, pass 1 + pass 2 | euler | **er_sde** |
| PASS 2 sigmas | beta, 4 steps, denoise 0.25 | **manual, 4 steps from 0.55** |

## Why it is faster
Step 1 runs at 0.2 MP instead of 0.5 MP: about 2.5x fewer tokens, and
attention cost grows faster than that. Step 2 costs the same as before
(still 4 steps at the same target size).

## Why it is sharper
In v1, pass 2 only repainted 25 %, so it could not add real detail and a big
jump came out soft. From 0.90 it drew new detail but re-acted the scene:
mouths moved on their own. Now it repaints from 0.55: the 3D latent upscaler
and the take keep the motion, and the model adds detail at full size.
Audio is still frozen from step 1 and the colour fix + FINISHING still run.

## Shift 6
Lower shift spends more of the steps on detail instead of rough layout,
which suits the small 0.2 MP draft.
Motion looks weak or messy? Set it back to 12.

## Want the v1 behaviour?
`megapixels` 0.5, SIGMA SHIFT node bypassed (Ctrl+B), samplers `euler`, and
the `gentle` sigmas preset from the pass 2 READ ME.

nodes.title: GIỮ CHI TIẾT THAM CHIẾU
widgets_values:
Nhánh B dùng vùng tham chiếu riêng 992×1792; video lấy kích thước từ latent rỗng theo bộ chọn độ phân giải. Vì vậy ảnh sheet không bị co chỉ theo bản nháp 0.2 MP.
Vùng tham chiếu lớn làm tăng token ở cả hai bước. Nếu chậm/OOM, giảm còn 544×960 hoặc dùng ít sheet hơn. Không tự giảm độ phân giải storyboard khi các ô đã quá nhỏ.

widgets_values_named.text:
# Soft faces - what was fixed

| what | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| PATH B reference area | 960 x 544 | **1792 x 992, automatic** |
| PASS 2 - SIGMAS | `0.9035, 0.8000, 0.6316, 0.3158, 0.0000` | `0.5500, 0.4200, 0.3158, 0.1579, 0.0000` |
| FINISHING | +0.35 at radius 0.12 | **+0.55 at radius 0.2** |
| VIDEO OUT | h264 auto (crf 18) | **h264 re-encode, crf 12** |

## Why faces were soft
- **References.** A 1664x2208 character sheet was cut to 640x832, so each face
  in it was about 100 px wide, and pass 2 reused that small copy. Now the
  face is about 180 px.
- **Last step.** The sampler's final image is one prediction from the last
  sigma. From 0.3158 that is a blurred guess. From 0.1579 it keeps fine skin
  detail. Still 4 steps, so pass 2 does not gain steps.
- **Saving.** crf 18 throws away faint skin texture. crf 12 keeps it, and files
  get about 2-3x bigger.

## Using it
- **Run step 1 again.** Old takes keep their small references.
- Bigger references ride along on every step: step 1 took 28% longer in a real
  run at 0.5 MP. Too slow, or out of memory? Use fewer reference images.
- Pass 2 starts at 0.55 so faces, mouths and motion stay as in the draft.
- Nothing to set. Every reference is sized automatically, at any pass 1 size,
  and small images are never enlarged.
- Turn any reference on or off with Ctrl+B on the image.
- PATH B `width` and `height` only size the references now. The video size
  still comes from **resolution + aspect ratio**.
- Faces in wide shots stay small: this helps close-ups the most.

widgets_values:
Chạy CHECK.bat sau khi START.bat đã mở server. CHECK chỉ xác minh node/model/ảnh/schema, không thay thế một lần render GPU.
Prompt do skill xuất dùng <Asset:ID>; PREPARE đổi thành <Picture n> theo ảnh thực. Không dán prompt chưa thay token vào node video.
